title: What happened in AI — Nov 2, 2026
intro: Agent builders spent the day on containment: Uber's MCP gateway and four new sandbox, kernel, and signature tools all enforce permissions outside the prompt.
DeepSeek open-sourced a coding agent that starts work from team chats, and Nvidia published two DGX Spark inference efforts.
highlights: Uber's MCP gateway governs 800+ servers and 5,000+ agent tools.
Deedglass caught an agent reporting 1 updated row when Postgres changed 301.
DeepSeek open-sourced Super-Agent, a coding agent that watches team chats.
Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU for native PyTorch on TPUs.
SemiAnalysis launched GDPx and OpenAI launched LifeVal as agent benchmarks.

categories.name: Agent harness and context design
categories.summary: Builders are converging on one loop-plus-sandbox architecture, and the open problems have moved to context, memory, and cross-device state.

articles.title: New context engineering challenges in late 2026
articles.summary: LangChain argues the LLM-in-a-loop-with-tools-in-a-sandbox architecture has converged and lists the context-engineering problems that remain.

articles.title: Article: Systemic Approach to Memory, Knowledge, and Context in Agentic AI Architectures
articles.summary: InfoQ article lays out a systemic approach to memory, knowledge, and context in agentic architectures.

articles.title: Show HN: Skep – live cross-device sessions for AI coding agents
articles.summary: Skep opens live join-code sessions so peers can share one task while each runs their own agent (Claude Code, Codex, Pi).

articles.title: Show HN: AgentTM – A time-travel debugger for AI coding agents built in Go
articles.summary: AgentTM records AgentTM-managed Codex runs in SQLite with baseline and final workspace checkpoints, so you can replay what an agent changed.

articles.title: Show HN: Rufous – Agent attuned to small models
articles.summary: Rufous is an agent harness built for 2B–12B models running locally, in an editor or a web UI.

categories.name: Agent permissions enforced outside the prompt
categories.summary: Four new tools and one gateway move agent access control into sandboxes, kernels, signatures, and verification instead of prompt instructions.

articles.title: Uber Builds MCP Gateway to Govern Access to 800+ Servers and 5,000+ AI Agent Tools
articles.summary: Uber built an MCP gateway to govern access to 800+ MCP servers and 5,000+ agent tools.

articles.title: Show HN: Maat – AI agents that can diagnose Ubuntu but can't change it
articles.summary: Maat gives agents a kernel-confined MCP server for diagnosing Ubuntu; fixes need polkit approval and leave a tamper-evident audit trail.

articles.title: Show HN: Deedglass – An agent said it updated 1 row; Postgres changed 301
articles.summary: Deedglass compares what an agent reported against what actually changed in Postgres (one reported row versus 301 changed) and seals each action as a signed record.

articles.title: Lyngvi – A Hardened Sandbox for AI
articles.summary: Lyngvi runs coding agents in a hardened sandbox that never exposes credentials, git history, or a route to the internet.

articles.title: Show HN: Arken – cryptographic identity for AI agents calling MCP servers/APIs
articles.summary: Arken proposes DID-signature identity so agents authenticate to MCP servers and APIs without passwords or sessions.

articles.title: Secure AI Agents with Hazmat Suits, Not Self-Defense Classes
articles.summary: Infisical argues agent security needs containment (the hazmat suit) rather than only trying to anticipate every attack.

categories.name: DeepSeek open-sources a proactive coding agent
categories.summary: DeepSeek released a research prototype coding agent that picks up work by watching team chats instead of waiting for prompts.

articles.title: DeepSeek open-sources Super-Agent, a coding agent that watches team chats for work
articles.summary: DeepSeek open-sources Super-Agent, a coding agent that monitors team chats and starts work from them.

articles.title: DeepSeek team open-sources proactive coding agent research prototype
articles.summary: TechNode reports the release as a proactive coding-agent research prototype from the DeepSeek team.

categories.name: Local and low-level inference
categories.summary: Two Nvidia-hosted projects target DGX Spark's memory-bound decoding, and Google and Meta put PyTorch natively on TPUs.

articles.title: Optimizing 124B MoE inference on a single Nvidia DGX Spark
articles.summary: Nvidia profiles Ling-3.0-flash decoding on DGX Spark as memory-bound and targets the MoE computation and output-layer projection.

articles.title: Flare, Nvidia's DGX Spark Inference Engine
articles.summary: Nvidia's Flare is a research-prototype local inference server for SM120/SM121 GPUs, aimed at long conversations and repeated tool calls.

articles.title: Google and Meta Open-source TorchTPU to Bring Native PyTorch Support to Google TPUs
articles.summary: Google and Meta open-source TorchTPU, bringing native PyTorch support to Google TPUs.

articles.title: Lakebase Postgres is now generally available on Google Cloud
articles.summary: Databricks made Lakebase Postgres generally available on Google Cloud, with compute separated from storage for agentic workloads.

categories.name: Benchmarks and compute economics
categories.summary: New benchmarks target economically valuable agent work, while the compute-glut debate leans on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash pricing.

articles.title: GDPx: Measuring Frontier Model Capabilities Across the Most Valuable Domains
articles.summary: SemiAnalysis introduces GDPx, a benchmark of the highest-value domains for frontier agentic capability.

articles.title: LifeVal
articles.summary: OpenAI's LifeVal benchmarks AI on everyday tasks such as finding childcare and handling government paperwork.

articles.title: Jevons paradox is lazy analysis: Evaluating the risk of AI overbuilding
articles.summary: A widely shared estimate argues next year's online compute would need about $2.5T of revenue even at DeepSeek V4.1 Flash rates, and the author is revising it.

articles.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
articles.summary: OpenAI's Grid Protectors Program works with utilities so future compute campuses protect grid reliability and consumer electricity costs.
